"If I had not existed, someone else would have written me, Hemingway, Dostoyevsky, all of us. Proof of that is that there are about three candidates for the authorship of Shakespeareâ€™s plays. But what is important is Hamlet and A Midsummer Nightâ€™s Dream, not who wrote them, but that somebody did. The artist is of no importance. Only what he creates is important, since there is nothing new to be said. Shakespeare, Balzac, Homer have all written about the same things, and if they had lived one thousand or two thousand years longer, the publishers wouldnâ€™t have needed anyone since."

Thoughts?

I think on the one hand, his main point is correct; the end product is ultimately what is important, not just who wrote it. A genius piece of writing should be genius regardless of its author.

But I don't think the last part of what he said is right, because I don't think anyone can effectively assume any style. Even in a thousand years it may be that Shakespeare would never be able to innovate the kind of writing that Faulkner used, or at least that he never actually would write like that even if he were capable of it. I guess from my perspective it's not so hard to take a crack at any story for anyone, but if I tried to write the Sound and the Fury it would come out a lot different than when Faulkner did it, and that difference is important and reflects the significance of the artist.

If you like something, you're passionate about it. It's really that simple. The 70s/80s and even 90s was a great time to be a kid. The 80s were full of these adventurous movies that kids (of all ages) connected deeply with.

Every thing I can think of that i identified with as a kid, has been rebooted, watered down, twisted around into something perverse and attempted to be sold back to me, and if i snubbed my nose - whatever the reasons, then i was a hipster..and now apparently a sexist.

I had to go to the comics store to find other people who did. I had a whole 2 friends that played some Marvel based RPG with me. JJ Abrams raped the fuck out of Star Trek, and now is letting Justin Lin have a turn or two fucking it's rotting corpse.
